goal: A peptide archive wants to compare coordinate completeness across the two attached deposits. What denominator should a curator use for each? Measure the coverage of the deposited chains, explain how end groups and residue annotations affect the comparison, and identify anything the observations cannot establish.

operation.reason: Both deposits have complete coverage of declared positions and amino-acid backbones in every submitted model. The original terminal and residue annotations explain the difference in denominators.
unresolved: Local coordinate precision, per-atom restraint support and side-chain atom completeness require separate assessments.

The counts and annotations leave sample stereochemistry, enantiomeric purity, solution protonation, unrecorded modifications, conformational populations, activity and prediction confidence unverified.

final_decision.rationale: The completed inventory checked the original sequence, chemistry, linkage and atom-site records and agrees with the coverage tables model by model. Chignolin assigns OXT to the final glycine. The tryptophan zipper numbers the terminal NH2 separately, includes coordinates for its nitrogen and bonds that nitrogen to the last lysine carbonyl. Those records account for both denominators. The two readings of each file agree, and further counts of those files would add no independent information about the sample.

post_read_actions.rationale: The measured fractions agree with a direct count of the original atom sites in every deposited model. Each declared position has a positive-occupancy heavy atom, and every amino acid has N, CA, C and O. Chignolin assigns its terminal oxygen to glycine. The tryptophan zipper gives its terminal amide a separate position and explicitly bonds its nitrogen to the terminal lysine carbonyl. Publish the two archive findings and await the commissioned independent inventory of the original annotations before final closure. Repeating the coordinate measurements would add no new observation.
